- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., 0.00 or -1.00) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below model output.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots downward — cap forecast decline to 5–8% below peak.  
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., 0.67+), model tends to overestimate future prices — apply downward bias of 3–7% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust — force a 1–3 day mean reversion correction toward historical 14-day moving average.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates true price by 2–5% in early days (e.g., day 1–7) — add 2–4% upward bias to first 7 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model exhibits high variance — use 14-day rolling mean as anchor for correction.
